Wait, there's an issue in my step() function. Let me trace the direction-change logic:

```js
while (inputQueue.length > 0) {
  const next = inputQueue.shift();
  if (next.x !== -dir.x || next.y !== -dir.y) {
    if (next.x !== dir.x || next.y !== dir.y) {
      dir = next;
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

This pops inputs. For each input:
- If it's NOT the exact reverse of dir: check if it's different from current dir; if so, apply and break. If it's the same as dir, continue the loop (consume next).
- If it IS the reverse, it's discarded silently (loop continues).

Hmm, wait: `next.x !== -dir.x || next.y !== -dir.y` — this is true unless BOTH next.x === -dir.x AND next.y === -dir.y. Since dir is a unit vector (one of x/y is 0), reverse of {x:1,y:0} is {x:-1,y:0}. So if next={x:-1,y:0}: -dir.x=-1, -dir.y=-0=0. next.x===-dir.x ✓ and next.y===-dir.y ✓, so condition false → discarded. Good.

If next = same as dir: next.x !== -dir.x is true (e.g. 1 !== -1), so enters the if. Then next.x !== dir.x false, next.y !== dir.y false → doesn't apply, doesn't break, continues. So same-direction inputs are consumed. OK.

If next is perpendicular: applies and breaks. Good.

Edge case: two quick inputs like dir=right, queue=[up, left]. Consume up → apply, dir=up, break. Next step: consume left → is left reverse of up? Reverse of up{0,-1} is down{0,1}. Left ≠ down → apply dir=left. Good — this handles the classic "right → up → left" fast turn within two steps.
